turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Hello? Can you hear me? I'm on the train, so I might drop.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: We can hear you, Yusuf. A bit of echo, but fine. Thandiwe, Torsten, you're both here?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Yes, hi.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Here.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Good. So we meet Brightwater Analytics tomorrow at ten, and I want us to agree on a position today, so we don't negotiate against each other in front of them. Yusuf, you've been talking to Oluwaseun Adebayo. Where are we?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Not in a great place, Camille. Their latest offer is four hundred and twenty thousand euros a year, on a three-year term, with a seven percent increase every year. So in the third year we'd be paying almost four hundred and eighty thousand. And they want all three years committed up front.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Seven percent a year? That's ambitious.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Oluwaseun says it reflects their data costs. I think it reflects that they know we need them.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: And what do you want to aim for?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: I'd open at three hundred and fifty thousand, increases capped at three percent, and two years with an option for a third. And I'd mention Horizon. Horizon quoted us two hundred and ninety thousand for a similar package.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Similar is generous, Yusuf.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Go on, Thandiwe.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Horizon has five years of history. We need ten. The whole forecasting model is trained on ten years, and five doesn't even include the last downturn. And their refresh is weekly, we need daily. So it isn't a similar package, it's a different product, and Oluwaseun knows that perfectly well.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Of course he knows. That doesn't mean we can't use it. You always want an alternative on the table, even a weak one.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: But if we threaten to walk to Horizon and he calls our bluff, what then? We look silly and we've lost a week.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: We don't threaten. We mention. There's a difference.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Thandiwe, honestly, if Brightwater walked away tomorrow, could we live with Horizon for a year?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Technically, yes. The forecasts would be noticeably worse, and my team would spend two months rebuilding pipelines. I'd really rather not.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: So Horizon is a real alternative. Just an expensive one, in a different way.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: That's all I need. Thandiwe, I promise I won't oversell it.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Fine. Just don't say similar.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Okay, okay. I'll say cheaper.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Torsten, you've been quiet. What about security?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: I've got three problems, and none of them is about price. First, they want to deliver files through a shared folder with one password for everyone. Not acceptable for this data. Second, their standard terms say they'll tell us about a breach within seventy-two hours. I want twenty-four. Third, part of their processing runs outside Europe, and the contract doesn't say where. I want the data kept in Europe, in writing, and a right to audit them once a year.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Twenty-four hours, they'll never accept.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Then forty-eight. But not seventy-two.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Which of the three are must-haves for you, Torsten?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: The shared password and the data location. Those are blockers. I won't sign the risk review without them. The audit and the notification time, I can negotiate.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Torsten, how long would changes like that take on their side? We need the first delivery before next quarter starts. If security holds up the signature, my team sits idle for a month.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: That's not on me, Thandiwe. If they can't deliver securely, the delay is theirs.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: I'm not blaming you. I'm saying the deadline is real.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Then say so in the email to Oluwaseun. The sooner they know, the sooner they fix it.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Okay, that's actually a good idea. We send the security requirements before the meeting, not during it. Then tomorrow is about price and scope.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: I'd prefer that too. If security comes up in the room, Oluwaseun will try to trade Lindqvist's list against price.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Now the numbers. Yusuf, what's our walk-away?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Four hundred thousand in the first year, increases capped at four percent.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Camille, can I ask for something in exchange? If we go up to four hundred, I want the daily refresh included. Right now it's an add-on, thirty thousand extra.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Thirty thousand on top? I didn't see that in the last offer.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Page eleven, in the appendix. Small print.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Of course it is. Thandiwe Mahlangu, reading the small print so I don't have to. Okay, that changes my maths.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: So let me propose a position. We open at three hundred and fifty thousand, with daily refresh and ten years of history included. Target three hundred and eighty. Walk-away four hundred, increases capped at four percent. Two years plus an option for a third. Horizon gets mentioned once, as an alternative we've priced, no details. Does that work for everyone?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Works for me.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Yes, as long as the refresh is in.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Fine, Camille, if the security email goes first.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Good. Who's in the room tomorrow? I'd like Yusuf to lead.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Happy to. Thandiwe, can you join for the first half hour, for scope? Then you can drop off before we talk money.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Yes, I'll do the scope part.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: And I'll join at the end, for the decision. Torsten, you don't need to be there if your email is clear.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Good, because I'm not very diplomatic at ten in the morning.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: We noticed.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Okay, actions. Torsten, the security requirements to Oluwaseun Adebayo, copying Yusuf Demirci, by six tonight.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: By six. Shared folder, data location, audit, notification. In that order.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Yusuf, can you get Horizon's quote in writing before tomorrow? So it's real if we mention it.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: I'll ask them this afternoon. If it doesn't arrive in time, I won't mention Horizon at all.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Good. Thandiwe, one page on what your team needs from Brightwater, history, refresh, formats, to Yusuf tonight.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Um, tonight's tight, but yes. By nine.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: And I'll brief our finance director so she's not surprised if we land at four hundred. Anything else?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: One thing. If Oluwaseun pushes for a decision in the room, we don't give one. We say we'll come back by Friday.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Agreed. Friday. Thanks, everyone. Yusuf, good luck with the train.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Thanks, Camille. I'm going into a tunnel, so, bye!
